stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria and null spec for a complex multi-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature. Openspec must first elaborate requirements and propose ACs; speckit then hardens testability, security, and edge cases. High priority due to real-time rendering complexity and complete lack of existing specification.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — no live preview integration exists. The useContent hook (236 callers) is the single choke point for all content fetching; live preview must attach there. Contentstack provides a live-preview SDK that emits real-time content updates via a WebSocket/polling mechanism; our code must subscribe to those events and merge updated content into the existing getContentByKey flow. Verification criteria are framed at our boundary since contentstack.io is unreachable at test time.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria list with only a contextual note. I created the full set from scratch based on the story title, technical note files, and openspec's note about Contentstack's live-preview SDK. Key design decisions: (1) AC1-2 cover the core happy path and the non-active-mode regression guard. (2) AC3-4 cover connection lifecycle (drop + reconnect) since WebSocket/polling connections are inherently unreliable. (3) AC5-6 cover edge cases for malformed data and irrelevant keys. (4) AC7 covers rapid-fire concurrent updates, a common race condition with real-time systems. (5) AC8 adds a security criterion — origin validation — since live preview opens a real-time channel that could be spoofed. (6) AC9 adds an accessibility criterion — ARIA live regions — required by WCAG for dynamically updating content. (7) AC10 covers subscription cleanup on unmount to prevent memory leaks, critical given useContent's 236 callers. (8) AC11-13 tie the feature to the specific files named in technical notes (ContentstackLink, contentCard, catch-all page). (9) AC14 covers the timeout edge case. (10) AC15 covers navigation resilience. I could not review the actual file contents of useContent.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, or [[...slug]].tsx — my criteria are based on file names and paths alone. If the contentCard interface or ContentstackLink component have specific constraints not inferable from their names, those criteria may need adjustment.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value. Openspec identified the architectural integration point (useContent hook, 236 callers) and the Contentstack live-preview SDK mechanism — strong technical context for a story with zero prior specification. Speckit then leveraged that context to construct a comprehensive 15-criterion AC set covering happy path, connection lifecycle, edge cases, security (origin validation), accessibility (ARIA live regions), and cleanup — none of which overlapped with openspec's contribution. However, two concerns warrant human review: (1) Speckit explicitly states it could not read the actual source files (useContent.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, [[...slug]].tsx) and derived criteria from file names and paths alone — criteria built without code inspection risk misalignment with real interface constraints. (2) Metadata inconsistency: speckit reports acceptanceChanged=false despite stating it created the full AC set 'from scratch,' which may indicate the delta was not actually persisted or the recording pipeline has a bug. A human should verify whether the generated ACs were applied to the story and validate them against the actual source files.
